verdict.rationale: Anytime Mailbox documents self-service forwarding: users can request with a few taps from a phone app or web portal that a letter or package be forwarded to another address, domestically or internationally, rather than emailing support. Nothing in the evidence shows the richer parts of the story. The 'Additional Recipient' article concerns who receives mail at the mailbox, not saved forwarding destinations, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: rule-based/automatic forwarding, saved forwarding recipients/address book, carrier selection, cost quote shown before confirming, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an operator, I can forward mail with rules or one click — saved recipients, carrier choice, and cost shown before I confirm — rather than emailing support

citations.quote: With a few taps, you can request that the operator open and scan a letter's contents, forward mail or a package to a different address, or shred junk mail.
Redirect postal mail and parcels to a secure forwarding address and manage them remotely from a phone app or web portal.
Forward letters and packages anywhere, domestically or internationally.
